templates.header:
## {emoji} {bot_name} — PR Review

Hi @{author}! I checked this pull request automatically. Here is my verdict:
templates.verdict_pass:
### ✅ Looks good!

All automated checks passed. A maintainer will review your changes soon thanks for contributing! 💜
templates.verdict_fail:
### ❌ Not ready yet

Some checks did not pass. Please fix the points marked with ❌ below and I will re-check automatically on your next push or edit.
templates.verdict_warn:
### ⚠️ Looks okay, with remarks

No blocking problems, but please take a look at the ⚠️ items below.
templates.footer: --- {emoji} I am not a human I re-run on every push and edit. Configure me in .github/parsecore-bot/config.json. Override switches: [skip-comment-check], [skip-docs] in the PR description.

title.fail: PR title must follow Conventional Commits: `type(scope): subject` e.g. `fix(pp): correct taiko convert scroll speed`. Allowed types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, chore, revert. Allowed scopes: beatmap, mods, pp, ci, packaging.

template.fail: Please fill out the PR template: write a **Summary**, tick at least one **Type of Change**, and complete the **Checklist**.

parity.pass: Parity section provided for Performance changes
parity.fail: This PR touches `parsecore/Performance/` but the **Parity** section is empty or `N/A`. Please state which official reference code (ppy/osu file + version) the change mirrors and confirm the parity suite passes with **zero differences**.
parity.skip: No `parsecore/Performance/` changes parity statement not required

comment_policy.pass: No inline comments added to parsecore code
comment_policy.fail: This PR adds `#` comments inside `parsecore/`. Inline comments are discouraged — put explanations in the function's docstring (Google style) instead. Add `[skip-comment-check]` to the PR description if this is a false positive.

size.fail: This PR adds more than {limit} lines. Consider splitting it into smaller, focused PRs large diffs slow down review and increase parity risk.
